November 3, 2026

US has secretly struck Iran in recent weeks, report says

tags: war, politics, media
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy

The Wall Street Journal reported that the United States attacked Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, described as the latest in a series of limited strikes carried out secretly in recent weeks. The report came as President Trump told reporters there had been no fighting for months and promoted the possibility of a diplomatic deal. The number of casualties is unknown, as is whether further strikes are planned. Journalists have not been embedded with US forces during this period.

Trump says US will end $4 billion in annual aid to Israel

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

In a Fox News interview, President Trump said the United States will stop providing Israel with roughly $4 billion a year in aid at the end of the year, while Israel will still be able to purchase American weapons. Trump said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu raised the idea himself and that the two had discussed it for a couple of years, arguing Israel no longer needs the money. Asked whether the figure referred to military hardware or cash, Trump said it covered aid in any form, describing it as barter, military aid or cash. He also cited US aid to Israel as a campaign issue for Democrats, naming Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

Courts reject Trump administration election challenges across the country

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Supreme Court rejected an administration appeal seeking to set aside about 20,000 California ballots said to have been cast by non-citizens, ruling within hours and without waiting for a response from California or recording any dissents. The Ninth Circuit separately rejected an attempt to pressure state election officials with threats of prosecution, and District Judge Tanya Chutkan blocked an effort to obtain state voter rolls. A federal judge also barred the administration from sending error-filled federal lists of supposed non-citizen voters to state and local election administrators, in a case litigated by Democracy Forward.

Whistleblowers describe conflicting ICE orders around election day

tags: immigration, politics, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

DHS whistleblowers said Homeland Security Investigations agents were ordered to take part in a voter fraud crackdown in blue states in the final hours before the midterms, with investigators reassigned from child exploitation and weapons trafficking cases to execute last-minute arrest warrants. Sources raised internal concerns about Hatch Act violations and said inadequate preparation time created safety risks. Separately, ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations officers in major cities were reportedly told through internal leadership channels and word of mouth to halt all enforcement operations on election day. The origin of the stand-down order and whether all ICE regions will follow it are unclear.

Trump says he would preemptively pardon Musk and White House aides

tags: politics, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

President Trump said he would issue preemptive pardons to Elon Musk and White House aides if Democrats take the House, telling a New York Post podcast that "we'll have to protect them." Democrats have signalled they would open investigations into Musk's DOGE work and federal contracts if they win control of Congress.

Justice Department deploys more than a thousand election monitors

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Justice Department released its list of locations where it is sending over a thousand election monitors across the country. The deployments are concentrated in heavily Democratic areas and places with high Hispanic and Black turnout. The monitors are not FBI or ICE agents and have no authority to interfere with voting.

Trump raises prospect of further Iran strikes in election day interview

tags: politics, war, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

In a Fox News interview on election day, President Trump said he was not looking to kill large numbers of people in Iran but would if he had to, calling the earlier military action a necessary detour to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and describing a recent strike as a minor attack rather than a war. He also joked that he could move to Israel and become prime minister, citing high approval ratings there. He promoted the construction of new data centers and criticised former President Obama and Democrats before the interview was cut off.

Mike Johnson tells donors he runs a "protection program"

tags: politics, legal
sources: @carolinegleich

In footage of remarks to donors, House Speaker Mike Johnson warned that if Republicans lose the midterms, Democrats would turn every congressional committee into an investigative body targeting the president's family, cabinet, donors and friends. He told the room that half of those present would be targeted and said, "I run the protection program. I'll take care of you." The majority party controls committee chairs, subpoenas and what Congress investigates.

Ten ballot measures on the line in the midterms

tags: politics, legal, health
sources: @groundnews

Voters are deciding a range of state ballot measures alongside congressional races. California's Proposition 40 would create the first US tax on billionaire wealth, a one-time 5% levy on net worth above $1 billion affecting about 250 people, with 90% of revenue for health care, while Proposition 39 would require voter ID at the polls. Other measures include Idaho's Proposition 1 to replace a near-total abortion ban with abortion rights up to viability, Montana's I-194 to bar corporate and dark money spending in state elections, Virginia's Question 3 to restore voting rights to people leaving prison, Colorado measures on mandatory life sentences for child sex trafficking and transgender participation in school sports, Massachusetts' Question 8 to repeal recreational marijuana sales, and Alaska's Ballot Measure 2 on ending ranked choice voting.

Judge dismisses DOJ suit over Alaska Senate certification

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

A federal judge rejected the administration's effort to stop Alaska from certifying a Senate election defeat for Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. The lawsuit argued that another candidate, Daniel J. Sullivan, could confuse voters choosing between the incumbent and Democrat Mary Peltola. US District Judge Sharon Gleason found no workable remedy with ballots already prepared and voting scheduled, and said the proposed ballot separation and investigation lacked a plan to protect voter privacy. A Justice Department spokesperson said the administration would appeal; Alaska's highest court had approved the second candidate's candidacy and the state's Republican administration supported dismissal.

Texas sets midterm early voting record

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Texas recorded 7,410,631 ballots cast by mail or in person before election day through Oct. 30, according to the secretary of state's office, a record for a state midterm. The total compares with about 5.5 million advance ballots in 2022 and fewer than 4.9 million in 2018, and represents 38.92% of the state's 19,041,684 registered voters. Early voting ended Friday, Oct. 30, with remaining voters going to the polls on Nov. 3.

Democrats flip Guam delegate seat in first result of the cycle

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Democrats secured their first win of the 2026 cycle, flipping Guam's non-voting delegate seat in the US House of Representatives. Alicia Garrido Limtiaco defeated Republican James Craig Moylan by just under three points. It is the first Democratic pickup in Congress this cycle.

Gas prices hit record high for an election day

tags: markets, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Fuel prices reached the highest level ever recorded on a US election day, with gasoline at $4.12 a gallon and diesel at $6.28 a gallon.

Administration moves to narrow workplace pregnancy accommodations

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

The administration is working to scale back workplace accommodations for pregnancy and reproductive health, limiting the reach of a 2022 law that provided accommodations such as bathroom and water breaks, relief from heavy lifting and time off for prenatal appointments, according to The New York Times. Conservatives have argued the rule enacted by the EEOC went beyond pregnancy to touch abortion and fertility treatment. The EEOC is planning to publish a narrowing of the conditions eligible for accommodations as soon as this month, which would restrict eligibility rather than eliminate the protections.

Republican infighting grows as Trump attacks Senate candidates online

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump spent the night before the midterms posting on Truth Social about various Senate candidates and races. Senior adviser Steve Bannon predicted an all-out civil war within the Republican Party after the elections.

Google to shut off search for schools that block its AI tools

tags: tech, education
sources: @groundnews

Google plans to switch off its AI services for K-12 students in 2027 unless school administrators authorise their use, and schools that block every AI function will lose student access to Google's search engine. Education vice president Chris Phillips told The New York Times that search and AI are deeply integrated and cannot be separated, meaning schools must accept AI in search for students to use Google for research. The policy covers Gemini, NotebookLM, Classroom's Gemini tools and Search, with implementation details to follow before the rollout.

Merz pledges more aid to Ukraine as Zelensky visits Berlin

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz promised additional aid and energy assistance to Ukraine as he hosted President Volodymyr Zelensky in Berlin, according to Reuters. Merz said Russian attacks in the Black Sea risk escalation and could trigger a global food crisis.

Trump devotes closing campaign appearance to the reflecting pool

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

President Trump's final press conference before the midterms, held in front of the reflecting pool, focused largely on repairs to the pool rather than the elections. He displayed photographs of algae, described the new piping and drainage, and said he had seriously considered renaming it the Trump reflecting pool before saying he was joking. Few supporters were present, with mostly National Park Service employees and reporters in attendance. On election day he posted on Truth Social complaining that the Daily Mail had misrepresented his joke and that media had not covered the event or his rally crowds adequately.

Don Jr. draws criticism over claim Democrats will make Ohio a state

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

While campaigning for Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio, Donald Trump Jr. said Democrats intend to pack the Supreme Court and make Ohio and Washington, DC states to secure permanent one-party rule. The reference to Ohio statehood circulated widely online and drew criticism.

Trump claims he could have won the Vietnam War in a week

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Campaigning in Dubuque, Iowa, on Nov. 1, President Trump said he could have won the Vietnam War in a single week, criticising the prolonged use of Agent Orange in forests instead of going after Ho Chi Minh City. Ho Chi Minh City was called Saigon during the war and was the capital of US-allied South Vietnam, while North Vietnam's capital was Hanoi. Trump received five deferments from military service during that period, four as a student and one for bone spurs.

Severe flooding turns Flagstaff streets into rivers

tags: climate
sources: @ericmoutsos

A storm caused extensive flooding across Arizona, with footage from Flagstaff showing a freeway and city streets running like rivers and a manhole cover blown off by water forced out of the drainage system. Observers described it as the worst flooding and the most water they had seen on that landscape. Similar conditions were reported from Colorado to Florida.
